### Assumptions

In [Example 1](#sec-example-1), say *Person 1* has job status $L_1$, *Person 2* has job status $L_2$ and *Person 3* has job status $L_3$. Each of these variables can only take on two values: “employed vs. unemployed.” Similarly, define $A_i$ as *Person $i$'s* dress (formal vs. informal), and $Y_i$ as their job offers (many vs. few). The job status measurement ($L_i$) precedes dress ($A_i$) in time, and dress precedes job offers ($Y_i$).

##### Assumption 1: No contagion


Under classic causal inference, we make the assumption of [no contagion](#def-no-spillover): no element of a covariate influences another element of the same covariate. With single-world independence, [equivalent measurements](#def-equivalence) taken across participants (e.g. $L_1$, $L_2$, and $L_3$) are then independent of each other given all prior measures, i.e.:


$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1 \perp L_2 \\
L_2 \perp L_3 \\
L_1 \perp L_3
\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
A_1 \perp A_2 | L_1, L_2, L_3\\
A_2 \perp A_3 | L_1, L_2, L_3 \\
A_1 \perp A_3 | L_1, L_2, L_3
\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_1 \perp Y_2 | L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3\\
Y_2 \perp Y_3 | L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3 \\
Y_1 \perp Y_3 | L_1, L_2, L_3, A_1, A_2, A_3
\end{aligned}
$$

This is shown in @fig-no-spillover-dag as the removal of arrows that connected the $L_i$'s, $A_i$'s and $Y_i$'s. In @eq-no-spillover-dag, the $L_i$'s are not functions of each other, the $A_i$'s are not functions of each other, and the $Y_i$'s are not functions of each other. i.e. Given all the measurements taken prior to a set of contemporaneous measures, the contemporaneous measures are independent. This follows from no contagion together with single-world independence, assumption (4) of the FFRCISTG; no assumption is made about the error terms.

{{< include ___figures/fig-no-spillover-dag.qmd >}}

{{< include ___equations/eq-no-spillover-dag.qmd >}}

##### Assumption 2: No interference


Classic causal inference makes the assumption of [no interference](#def-no-interference): no variable in one participant's unit is a parent of a non-equivalent variable in another participant's unit. This is shown as the absence of arrows that point from the $L_i$'s to $A_j$'s, the $L_i$'s to the $Y_j$'s and the $A_i$'s to the $Y_j$ for participants $i\neq j$ (see @fig-independence-dag).

This allows us to simplify the structural equation model so that each participant's measures are a function of only measures taken on them.


{{< include ___equations/eq-independence-dag-full.qmd >}}


##### Assumption 3: Identical structural distributions

Finally, we see above that the functions that generate observations $L_i$ are similar in structure to each other, as are the functions that generate $A_i$'s and $Y_i$s. We make the homogeneity assumption that the functions are [identical](#def-identical-distributions) to each other, and that the error terms of equivalent variables are identically distributed, $U_{L_1} \overset{d}{=} U_{L_2} \overset{d}{=} U_{L_3}$, and likewise for $A$ and $Y$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
 f_L &= f_{L_1} = f_{L_2} = f_{L_3} \\
 f_A &= f_{A_1} = f_{A_2} = f_{A_3} \\
 f_Y &= f_{Y_1} = f_{Y_2} = f_{Y_3}  \\
\end{aligned}
$$

##### Assumption 4: Single-world independence

Finally, we assume [single-world independence](#def-single-world), the causal assumption of the FFRCISTG: for every value of the nine variables, the one-step-ahead counterfactuals, each variable's value when its parents are set to their values there, are mutually independent. In Example 1, fixing $L_i = l$ and $A_i = a$ for every person, the variables $L_i$, $A_i^{(l)}$ and $Y_i^{(l, a)}$ are mutually independent, within and across persons. Nothing is assumed about the error terms. This is the assumption the identification argument below uses.
